blocks.text: **The task.** Given an integer array, answer many queries of the form "what is the sum of elements from index i to index j inclusive?" The array never changes.
The phrase "many queries" and "never changes" is the signal. Build once in the constructor, answer in O(1).
Negative numbers need no special handling. Subtraction undoes addition whatever the sign — which is exactly the property the pattern requires.
For Q queries the total is O(N + Q) instead of O(N x Q). With N and Q both 10,000 that is 20,000 operations rather than 100 million.

Prefix sums assume immutability — a single update invalidates every entry after it, costing O(N) to repair. If updates are frequent, you want a Fenwick tree or segment tree, which give O(log N) for both update and query.
